statements.text: Could you share USDA's plans for continuing this important investment in promoting advances in ag through AI technology?
statements.context: House Agriculture Committee hearing reviewing USDA research program implementation, specifically Title VII.

statements.text: What steps is the VA taking to monitor and keep up with the emerging research on artificial intelligence?
statements.context: House hearing on AI at the Department of Veterans Affairs, questioning a witness panel about the VA's approach to emerging AI research.

statements.text:
Started off the morning at @VetAffairsDems subcommittee hearing where my colleagues and I learned about the current and future uses of AI in @DeptVetAffairs health care.

Thanks to all panelists for discussing how we can use evolving tools to enhance health care access for all. https://t.co/IDsQ7yDNbW

Today, I attended a bipartisan roundtable discussion about AI and agriculture. Thanks to #IL13's own Dr. Vikram Adve for sharing his perspective as director of @UofIllinois' AIFARMS Institute, which explores how AI can improve agricultural productivity and sustainability! https://t.co/YdpPM53i1V

As the ranking member on the Technology Modernization Subcommittee, I am certainly excited by the potential of both AI and innovation. AI could improve some of VA's challenges through large language models and higher processing speeds. [...] Also, we as a committee and as Congress need to have a real conversation about AI policy and how to implement it safely. I am excited about the opportunities that AI presents. I am not convinced that VA is prepared to deploy this technology just yet.
statements.venue: House Veterans' Affairs Technology Modernization Subcommittee hearing, opening statement as ranking member

statements.text: AI has immense potential for agriculture, with digital innovations to help farmers increase efficiency, reduce costs and improve sustainability. I loved seeing some of these new technologies in action at @DigitalAgUIUC! https://t.co/wCQlv30JLO
Will the system require informed consent from the veteran before AI is used during their appointment?
statements.context: Representative Budzinski questioning VA officials during a House hearing on the VA EHRM program.

statements.text: What government structures are in place to ensure that any code added to VA's system is not going to have unintended consequences?
statements.context: House committee hearing on software licensing management, where the representative questions a witness about DOGE activities at the Department of Veterans Affairs.

statements.text: We want to be competing with China. And to do that in the AI race, we need to generate more energy. To compete on the AI issues, but also to build out those data centers that AI needs to really thrive.

GAO's Artificial Intelligence Accountability Framework notes the workforce is a key component to ensuring effective AI application. How does a highly skilled technical workforce ensure adequate scalability of AI applications and protection of veteran data?
statements.context: Representative Budzinski asks a follow-up question during a House subcommittee hearing on AI in VA healthcare.

statements.text: I have a number of concerns that I hope to address today, like the lack of regulation and governance structures and the need for better transparency around what data is involved in training such models.
statements.context: Opening statement at a House subcommittee oversight hearing on AI use at the Veterans Health Administration.

statements.text: Could you commit for me that the VA will never use AI, including chatbots, as a substitute for frontline staff responders for mental health crisis intervention?
statements.context: Representative Nikki Budzinski poses a question during a House subcommittee hearing on AI in Veterans Affairs healthcare.

statements.text: Okay. Other than that general awareness—for veterans, is there any way to kind of draw their attention to this so that they know that, you know, what their situation might be using to inform an AI model?
statements.context: Question from a House subcommittee hearing on AI in VA healthcare.

statements.text: Ms. Harris, could I ask, what risks are posed by using AI tools for use cases other than their intended purpose, like the use of chatbots that were developed for programs like Veterans Readiness and Employment (VR&E) or home loans and crisis intervention support?
statements.context: House subcommittee hearing on AI in VA care, where Rep. Budzinski questions a witness about off-label use of VA chatbots.

statements.text: Considering the efforts of this administration to limit what kind of data may be available in research data sets or in a veteran's medical file, do you believe that this will impact the efficacy of VA's AI tools?
statements.context: House subcommittee hearing on AI in Veterans Affairs healthcare, with a member questioning a witness about data restrictions and model bias.

statements.text: I worry that VHA's rushed to expand automation will lead to similar errors that could put patients at risk. Shifting gears, Mr. Worthington, how do you plan to measure accuracy of implemented and piloted AI tools?
statements.context: House hearing on VA use of AI, with the member questioning a witness about accuracy and safety of deployed tools.

statements.text: As it is currently funded and staffed, do you believe the VA is capable of implementing additional AI-use cases on top of these other modernization efforts that I have mentioned.
statements.context: Question posed during a House subcommittee hearing on AI use at the Department of Veterans Affairs.

statements.text: The @NewDemCoalition Innovation agenda is about driving growth and embracing new tech in ways that benefit hardworking Americans. For our 10th New Dems On the Road Stop, we met top tech leaders to talk AI, workforce development, and infrastructure to support the 21st century innovation economy.

I think we need more data-driven policy proposals, and I'm working on those in Washington to better articulate what the impacts are going to be so that we can help to prepare. I think that — you know, that's kind of what mostly concerns me about AI, but I think that to say that AI is going away, I think that is an irresponsible position to take.
statements.venue: The 21st Show, Illinois Public Media interview

statements.text: But we need regulation, and what you're seeing right now is — because the federal government has been unable to come together on a federal regulatory framework that works — you're seeing states ... Illinois has really led the way in putting some safeguards in place as it relates to AI.
statements.venue: The 21st Show, Illinois Public Media interview

statements.text: I particularly care about the workforce side, and those are the issues that I've been particularly leaning in on. And some of the reason why I raised that is we don't exactly know.
statements.venue: The 21st Show, Illinois Public Media interview

statements.text: As your Member of Congress, I cannot and will not support the construction of data centers in our communities until developers can demonstrate how they will cover 100% of the costs required to power their facilities, without shifting any costs to consumers or threatening the reliability of our electrical grid. Moreover, developers need to provide a clear plan for meeting their water needs without increasing rates for communities or jeopardizing the safety of the water supply.
statements.venue: Belleville News-Democrat candidate questionnaire on data centers

statements.text: Nobody’s voice or likeness should be used without their consent. @RepBeccaB is right to push for guidelines surrounding AI usage in campaigns. The NO FAKES Act is what we need to bring accountability. https://t.co/foWjQlXOjv
statements.quoted:
A political opponent recently posted a deepfake video of me on social media. It was generated using AI and fabricated my voice and image to put words in my mouth. While it represents a new - and dangerous - low, it was not unpredictable.

It just drives home why we need to act now to give people protections against unauthorized AI replicas of their name and likeness. Let’s start by passing my NO FAKES Act.

statements.text: I hear from employees that the so-called fixes that VA has pushed, like automation and pilots of artificial intelligence tools, often produce incorrect information, compounding issues and slowing production,
statements.venue: House VA subcommittee hearing, reported by Nextgov

statements.text:
Recent cyberattacks and security incidents involving AI agents, alongside warnings about loss of control from those who have worked in AI, cannot be ignored. 
Congress should act now to ensure that this technology is advancing responsibly, within strict guardrails, with the safety of the American people as our top priority.
statements.quoted: OpenAI breach of Australian government linked to wider AI hacking campaign https://t.co/o4PEQmfQhg
